query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is intended to retain the favorable mechanical performance of the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy while reducing cost and preserving a useful strength–ductility balance. Existing FeNiCrMn research has focused mainly on corrosion rather than dynamic loading. Molecular-dynamics studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys have examined temperature, strain rate, cracking, voids, and compositional variation, demonstrating condition-dependent mechanical responses, but they do not establish how to improve FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading. Given the constraints of remaining Co-free, controlling cost, and retaining balanced strength and ductility, what single intervention could improve the dynamic mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn over a defined range of temperatures and strain rates? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, the causal mechanism, a predicted outcome relative to unmodified FeNiCrMn, its boundary conditions, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy can be improved by introducing a small amount of Zr, which can enhance the solid solution strengthening and improve the mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast or annealed FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of Zr (e.g., 1-3 at.%)
generation.conditions: Dynamic loading, various temperatures (e.g., room temperature to 800°C) and strain rates (e.g., 0.001-0.1 s^-1)
generation.structural_mediator: Solid solution strengthening, grain refinement, and potential phase transformations
generation.mechanism: The addition of Zr can lead to solid solution strengthening, which can improve the mechanical properties of the FeNiCrMn alloy. The Zr atoms can also refine the grain size, which can enhance the strength and ductility. Additionally, the introduction of Zr can potentially lead to phase transformations, which can further improve the mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties, including increased strength, ductility, and toughness, under dynamic loading conditions
generation.boundary: Temperature range: room temperature to 800°C, strain rate range: 0.001-0.1 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Zr to be added, the optimal processing conditions, and the potential interactions between Zr and other alloying elements

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and dynamic loading experiments on FeNiCrMn alloys with and without Zr additions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Zr does not lead to improved mechanical properties under dynamic loading conditions, the hypothesis is falsified

Nanoindentation behavior of high entropy alloys with transformation-induced plasticity

Abstract: Nanoindentation of three metastable dual-phase high entropy alloys (HEAs) was performed to obtain their inherent elastoplastic deformation responses. Excellent combination of hardness and elastic modulus in as-cast condition confirmed that, their inherently higher strength compared to other HEAs reported in literature, can be attributed to alloy chemistry induced phase stability. Further, hardness of 8.28 GPa combined with modulus of 221.8 GPa was obtained in Fe-Mn-Co-Cr-Si-Cu HEA by annealing the as-cast material, which is the best hardness-modulus combination obtained to date in HEAs from nanoindentation. Microstructure and composition dependence of mechanical characteristics of nanoimprinted AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys

Abstract: Molecular dynamics is applied to explore the deformation mechanism and crystal structure development of the AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys under nanoimprinting. The influences of crystal structure, alloy composition, grain size, and twin boundary distance on the mechanical properties are carefully analyzed. The imprinting load indicates that the highest loading force is in ascending order with polycrystalline, nano-twinned (NT) polycrystalline, and monocrystalline. The change in alloy composition suggests that the imprinting force increases as the Al content in the alloy increases. The reverse Hall–Petch relation found for the polycrystalline structure, while the Hall–Petch and reverse Hall–Petch relations are discovered in the NT-polycrystalline, which is due to the interactions between the dislocations and grain/twin boundaries (GBs/TBs). Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
